items.title: Sources of Light
items.explanation: The Sun emits its own light and is the main natural source of light on Earth. Stars, lightning, fire, and certain animals also emit their own light. Objects that emit their own light are called luminous objects (like the Sun), while objects that do not emit light but reflect it are non-luminous objects (like the Moon). The Moon reflects sunlight; therefore, moonlight is reflected sunlight.

items.title: Types of Light Sources
items.explanation: Natural sources include the Sun, stars, lightning, and animals. Artificial sources include fire (using fuels like oil or gas), electric lamps, and LED lamps. LEDs are preferred because they consume less power, last longer, and reduce electricity bills.

items.title: Light Travels in a Straight Line
items.explanation: Experiments using matchboxes, torches, and bent pipes demonstrate that light travels in straight lines. When an object blocks the path of light, it creates a shadow because light cannot bend around corners.

items.title: Light Through Materials
items.explanation: Materials can be classified as transparent (allowing light to pass fully), translucent (allowing partial light passage), or opaque (blocking all light). A laser beam follows a straight path through water but can bend around corners in complex environments.
